svg.title: Stresemann’s Foreign Policy Recovery: Locarno, Geneva & Rhineland Evacuations (1924–29)
svg.desc: Historical GIS atlas map illustrating Gustav Stresemann’s diplomatic recovery of Weimar Germany (1924–29), contrasting the Guaranteed Western Frontier under the October 1925 Locarno Pact (guaranteed by Britain and Italy) against the Unfixed Eastern Frontier with Poland and Czechoslovakia (arbitration treaties only), alongside Geneva (1926 League of Nations Council seat), Paris (1928 Kellogg–Briand Pact), Berlin (1924 Dawes Plan, 1926 Treaty of Berlin with USSR, and 1929 Young Plan), and staged Allied Rhineland evacuations at Cologne (1926), Coblenz (1929), and Mainz (1930).

text.tspan: Fixed at Locarno • Backed by Britain & Italy
Voluntary western border peace • 1926 Nobel Prize
Arbitration only • Keeps peaceful revision open
Permanent Council seat restores great-power status
Germany & 64 states renounce war as policy

svg.text: EDEXCEL GCSE HISTORY • PAPER 3 (OPTION 31): WEIMAR & NAZI GERMANY, 1918–39
Stresemann’s Foreign Policy Recovery: Locarno, Geneva & Rhineland (1924–29)
Locarno (1925) guaranteed Western borders (unlocking League entry in 1926 & Rhineland evacuations) while keeping Eastern borders open to revision.
Dawes (1924) & Young (1929) cut reparations to £2bn via 800m mark US loans—leaving Germany "dancing on a volcano" before Oct 1929.
